items.title: What we know about Lufthansa's plan to cut 1,000 jobs in Frankfurt and Munich
items.summary: Lufthansa is set to slash 1,000 full-time jobs at its Frankfurt and Munich airport hubs, it emerged on Friday.

items.title: German metalworkers' union calls 24-hour strike for first time in eight years
items.summary: Work stoppages were affecting shipyards, suppliers and major automakers on Friday as metalworkers and electricians across Germany walked off the job for better pay.

items.title: Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs, citing ongoing losses — reports
items.summary: According to a letter obtained by the media, Lufthansa's executive board said the German company is losing €20 million every month. In addition to job cuts, operational cuts are also planned.

items.title: 'Fight for our future': Youth protesters to join forces across Europe
items.summary: Protesters across Europe are set to take to the streets on Friday in a show of cross-border solidarity, joining coordinated demonstrations against the rising cost of living, militarisation and other causes, in a bid to increase pressure on their governments.

items.title: German cabinet approves major custody and child support overhaul
items.summary: The Federal Cabinet has approved the biggest shake-up of child custody law in decades, alongside separate changes to the rules around child support payments. Here's what the reforms could mean for families in Germany.

items.title: Germany's conservatives launch another bid to tighten citizenship rules
items.summary: Germany’s main governing party is pushing changes that would severely limit dual-citizenship and tighten requirements to naturalise. The centre-left Social Democrats are said to be reviewing the plans.

items.title: Is it really 'impossible' to get fired in Germany?
items.summary: Germany is known for its strong employment protection laws. Perhaps that's why a myth has developed that once you secure a permanent employment contract, it's almost impossible for your employer to get rid of you. Is it true?

Federal Employment Agency 2027 Budget Focuses on Training Amid Deficit
items.summary: The Bundesagentur für Arbeit (Federal Employment Agency) approved its 2027 budget, projecting an 8.2 billion euro deficit to be covered by federal loans due to high unemployment. Despite administrative cuts, the agency allocated 4.2 billion euros for targeted further training and job placement programs to help job seekers enter the labor market.

items.title: Dr. Anna Robra takes over as chair of the BA administrative board
items.summary: Dr. Anna Robra has been elected as the new chair of the administrative board of the Bundesagentur für Arbeit (BA [Federal Employment Agency]). The leadership position rotates annually between employer and employee representatives. Robra emphasizes ongoing administrative reforms to help the BA focus on its core task of getting people into jobs.

Job Market for Academics: Higher Unemployment but Good Prospects
items.summary: Unemployment among university graduates in Germany reached 372,000 by August 2026, driven by economic slowdown and new technologies like AI. However, academics still face a low unemployment rate of 3.3 percent in 2025 and continue to find jobs faster than other groups. Over two million graduates secured employment in 2025, supported by high demand due to demographic changes.

Job Market Conditions Worsen for Apprenticeship Seekers in Germany
items.summary: Data from the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) for the 2025/26 advisory year shows a decline in registered training positions and an increase in applicants. As of September 30, 2026, 46,000 applicants remained unplaced while 48,000 positions were still vacant. Despite the tougher market, support services remain available for those seeking an apprenticeship.

items.title: IT Outage at Agentur für Arbeit: Extended Deadlines for Job Seekers
items.summary: Due to a technical failure at the Bundesagentur für Arbeit (Federal Employment Agency) between September 30 and October 4, 2026, job seekers who could not submit required notices online will face no disadvantages. Affected individuals can submit their missing notifications, such as jobseeker registrations, until October 9, 2026.

items.title: New AI voice assistant "Klara" launched by Bundesagentur für Arbeit
items.summary: The Federal Employment Agency has introduced "Klara," a new AI voice assistant for its SGB III service hotline, starting September 22, 2026. The assistant handles initial calls and answers standard questions in pilot regions to reduce wait times for the roughly 18 million annual callers. Klara does not make official employment decisions, which remain handled exclusively by human staff.
